```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6.5,
                      fig.height = 4, dpi = 80)
library(hyperutils)
```

The standard plots and tables of `hp_eda_plot()` and `hp_nca_plots()` cover
the usual needs. When a report asks for something else, `hp_custom_plot()` and
`hp_custom_table()` build it from a plain list of settings, for any data
frame. Because the description is a list, it can be printed, stored, reviewed
and reused, and the same list produces the same figure every time.

```{r data}
d <- hp_read_data(hp_example_file())
obs  <- hp_custom_prep(d, filter = "EVID == 0 & !is.na(DV)")
subj <- hp_custom_prep(d, filter = "EVID == 1", distinct = "ID")
```

## Plots

A plot is a list. The essentials are `geoms` (what to draw) and the mapping
of columns to `x`, `y`, `color`, `fill`, `shape`, `size`, `linetype`, `group`
and `label`. A mapping can be a column name or an R expression of the
columns, such as `"factor(DOSEGRP)"` or `"log10(DV)"`.

### Points, lines and a log axis

```{r spaghetti}
hp_custom_plot(obs, list(
  geoms = c("line", "point"), x = "TIME", y = "DV", group = "ID",
  color = "factor(DOSEGRP)", y_log = TRUE,
  x_title = "Time (h)", y_title = "Concentration (ng/mL)",
  legend_title = "Dose (mg)", title = "Individual profiles",
  hline = 0.5))
```

`hline` draws a reference line (here the limit of quantification); `vline`
and `abline` (a list of `c(intercept, slope)`) work the same way.

### Mean and spread at each time

The `errorbar` and `pointrange` geoms summarise `y` at each value of `x`.
`summary_error` chooses `"sd"` (default), `"sem"` or `"ci95"`.

```{r errorbar}
hp_custom_plot(obs, list(
  geoms = c("errorbar", "pointrange"), x = "TIME", y = "DV",
  color = "factor(DOSEGRP)", summary_error = "sd", y_log = TRUE,
  x_title = "Time (h)", y_title = "Mean concentration (ng/mL)",
  legend_title = "Dose (mg)"))
```

### Distributions

```{r box}
hp_custom_plot(subj, list(
  geoms = c("boxplot", "jitter"), x = "factor(DOSEGRP)", y = "WT",
  fill = "factor(DOSEGRP)", legend = "none", jitter = 0.15,
  x_title = "Dose group (mg)", y_title = "Body weight (kg)"))
```

```{r hist}
hp_custom_plot(subj, list(
  geoms = "histogram", x = "WT", fill = "factor(SEX)", nbins = 8,
  facet_wrap = "SEX", labels_both = TRUE, legend = "none",
  theme = "minimal", x_title = "Body weight (kg)"))
```

Other distribution geoms are `violin`, `density`, `ecdf` and `qq`.

```{r violin}
hp_custom_plot(subj, list(geoms = c("violin", "boxplot"), x = "factor(SEX)",
                          y = "AGE", fill = "factor(SEX)", bar_width = 0.15,
                          legend = "none", x_title = "Sex (0 = F, 1 = M)",
                          y_title = "Age (years)"))
```

### Relationships with a smoother

```{r smooth}
peak <- aggregate(DV ~ ID + WT + DOSEGRP, data = obs, FUN = max)
hp_custom_plot(peak, list(
  geoms = c("point", "smooth"), x = "WT", y = "DV", color = "factor(DOSEGRP)",
  smooth_se = TRUE, x_title = "Body weight (kg)", y_title = "Cmax (ng/mL)",
  legend_title = "Dose (mg)"))
```

`smooth` draws a straight line; set `smooth_loess = TRUE` for a loess curve
(with `span`). `smooth_se` adds the confidence band and `smooth_level` sets
its level.

### Bars and heat maps

`bar` counts rows, or summarises `y` with `summary_fun` when `y` is given.

```{r bar}
hp_custom_plot(subj, list(
  geoms = "bar", x = "factor(DOSEGRP)", y = "WT", summary_fun = "median",
  fill = "factor(SEX)", position = "dodge", legend_title = "Sex",
  x_title = "Dose group (mg)", y_title = "Median body weight (kg)"))
```

```{r tile}
cells <- aggregate(DV ~ TIME + DOSEGRP, data = obs, FUN = mean)
hp_custom_plot(cells, list(geoms = "tile", x = "factor(TIME)",
                           y = "factor(DOSEGRP)", fill = "log10(DV)",
                           x_title = "Time (h)", y_title = "Dose (mg)",
                           fill_title = "log10 mean DV", palette = "viridis"))
```

### One panel per group

`facet_wrap` splits by one or several columns, `facet_rows` and
`facet_cols` make a grid. `scales` frees the axes.

```{r facets}
hp_custom_plot(obs[obs$ID %in% 1:6, ], list(
  geoms = c("line", "point"), x = "TIME", y = "DV", facet_wrap = "ID",
  facet_ncol = 3, labels_both = TRUE, y_log = TRUE, scales = "free_y",
  legend = "none", x_title = "Time (h)", y_title = "Concentration (ng/mL)"))
```

### Look and feel

```{r look}
base <- list(geoms = c("line", "point"), x = "TIME", y = "DV", group = "ID",
             color = "factor(DOSEGRP)", y_log = TRUE)
hp_custom_plot(obs, c(base, list(
  theme = "bw", palette = "dark2", legend = "top", alpha = 0.6,
  title = "A bigger title", title_size = 14, subtitle = "with a subtitle",
  caption = "Source: example data", legend_title = "Dose (mg)")))
```

Themes are `"classic"` (default), `"minimal"`, `"bw"`, `"light"`, `"grey"` and
`"void"`. Palettes are `"okabe-ito"` (default, colour-blind safe),
`"tableau"`, `"set1"`, `"dark2"`, `"pastel"`, `"grey"` and `"viridis"`.

### The result is a ggplot

Because the return value is a ggplot object, anything ggplot2 offers can be
added afterwards, and the package theme can be added to any ggplot:

```{r extend}
p <- hp_custom_plot(obs, c(base, list(legend_title = "Dose (mg)")))
p + ggplot2::annotate("text", x = 12, y = 9, label = "Peak at 2 to 4 h", size = 3) +
  ggplot2::coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 48))
```

## Tables

A table is also a list, with a `kind`. The result is a data frame of text.

### Listing

```{r listing}
hp_custom_table(head(subj[, c("ID", "AMT", "WT", "AGE", "SEX")], 5),
                list(kind = "listing"))
```

### Summary statistics

```{r summary}
hp_custom_table(subj, list(
  kind = "summary", vars = c("WT", "AGE"), by = "SEX", total = TRUE,
  stats = c("n", "mean", "sd", "median", "min", "max")))
```

Available statistics are `n`, `nmiss`, `mean`, `sd`, `cv`, `sem`, `median`,
`min`, `max`, `q1`, `q3`, `p5`, `p95`, `geomean`, `gcv`, `mean_sd` and
`median_range`.

### Demographics

The baseline table of a clinical study report, with a column per group.
Variables with few values (here `SEX`) are categorical.

```{r demographics}
hp_custom_table(subj, list(
  kind = "demographics", vars = c("WT", "AGE", "SEX"), by = "DOSEGRP",
  total = TRUE, stats = c("mean_sd", "median_range")))
```

Use `continuous` and `categorical` to override the guess, `percent_digits`
for the percentages and `max_levels` for the number of distinct values up to
which a numeric column counts as categorical.

### Frequencies and cross-tabulations

```{r frequency}
hp_custom_table(subj, list(kind = "frequency", rows = "SEX", columns = "DOSEGRP",
                           percent = "column"))
```

`percent` is `"none"`, `"row"`, `"column"` or `"total"`.

### Pivot tables

A statistic of a value column, by rows and columns.

```{r pivot}
hp_custom_table(subj, list(kind = "pivot", rows = "SEX", columns = "DOSEGRP",
                           value = "WT", fun = "mean", total = TRUE))
```

### Correlations

```{r correlation}
hp_custom_table(subj, list(kind = "correlation", vars = c("WT", "AGE", "AMT")))
```

### Finishing touches

Any table can be renamed, trimmed and reshaped:

```{r finishing}
hp_custom_table(subj, list(
  kind = "summary", vars = c("WT", "AGE"), by = "SEX",
  stats = c("n", "mean", "sd"),
  rename = list(c("N", "Subjects"), c("SEX", "Sex (0 = F, 1 = M)")),
  decimals = 1))
```

`hide` drops columns, `na_text` replaces empty cells, and `transpose = TRUE`
swaps rows and columns.

## Putting a report page together

```{r page}
out <- file.path(tempdir(), "custom")
tab <- hp_custom_table(subj, list(kind = "demographics", vars = c("WT", "AGE", "SEX"),
                                  by = "DOSEGRP", total = TRUE))
fig <- hp_custom_plot(obs, c(base, list(legend_title = "Dose (mg)",
                                        x_title = "Time (h)",
                                        y_title = "Concentration (ng/mL)")))
files <- c(hp_save_table(tab, "demographics.csv", out),
           hp_save_plot(fig, "profiles", out, width = 6.5, height = 4, dpi = 72))
basename(files)
unlink(out, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Reference

The full list of plot and table settings is on the help pages
`?hp_custom_plot` and `?hp_custom_table`. For standard figures and tables of
a dataset see `vignette("exploratory-analysis")`.
